content: The Detroit Medical Center (DMC) is a non-profit healthcare organization based in Detroit, Michigan, that operates nine general and specialty hospitals in the southeastern region of the state. These hospitals provide a wide range of specialized medical services: 1. DMC Children’s Hospital of Michigan is the only pediatric Level I trauma center in southeast Michigan, offering advanced care for critically injured children. 2. DMC Detroit Receiving Hospital was Michigan’s first Level I trauma center, providing comprehensive emergency and trauma care. 3. DMC Harper University Hospital specializes in bariatric surgery, cardiology, vascular procedures, neurosurgery, neurology, and kidney and pancreas organ transplants. 4. DMC Huron Valley-Sinai Hospital, located in Oakland County, Michigan, offers a variety of general and specialized medical services. 5. DMC Hutzel Women’s Hospital focuses on obstetrics, infertility treatments, and gynecological care. 6. DMC Kresge Eye Institute is renowned for its expertise in ophthalmology and corneal transplantation. 7. DMC Michigan Orthopaedic Specialty Hospital provides advanced orthopedic care and surgical services. 8. DMC Rehabilitation Institute of Michigan specializes in rehabilitation medicine, including care for spinal cord injuries. 9. DMC Sinai-Grace Hospital is known for its expertise in total joint replacement surgery. The DMC is closely affiliated with the Karmanos Cancer Institute, a separate non-profit entity recognized for its excellence in cancer treatment and research. The Detroit Medical Center operates over 2,000 licensed hospital beds and employs more than 12,000 staff members, including 3,000 affiliated physicians. Many of its hospitals are staffed by physicians from the Wayne State University School of Medicine, the largest single-campus medical school in the United States. The DMC serves as the official healthcare provider for several professional sports teams, including the Detroit Tigers, Detroit Red Wings, Detroit Pistons, Detroit Shock, and the Detroit Belle Isle Grand Prix. It is fully accredited by the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations. Two DMC hospitals, Harper University Hospital and Sinai-Grace Hospital, are ranked in the top one percent nationwide for heart failure outcomes. This ranking, based on data from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Federal Department of Health and Human Services, places them among only 38 hospitals in the United States to exceed the national average in heart failure care. These rankings help the public evaluate hospital performance in treating specific conditions, such as heart failure and heart attacks. The DMC is the only health system in Michigan with two hospitals achieving this distinction. In 2007, the DMC was named to the Most Wired list by Hospitals & Health Networks magazine, which recognizes hospitals that excel in using information technology to improve healthcare quality. The DMC’s use of technology has been instrumental in enhancing quality, customer service, public health, safety, and operational efficiency. The DMC also received the prestigious “Best Practices in Infrastructure Management” award from Computerworld’s Infrastructure Management World. This award recognizes the DMC’s leadership in utilizing infrastructure management technology to improve healthcare delivery. The DMC is one of only two organizations nationwide to receive this honor annually. Michael E. Duggan, the former Wayne County Executive, served as the DMC’s president and CEO starting in January 2004. Emery King, a former journalist with WDIV, serves as the DMC’s Communications Director and oversees the Emery King Healthcare Video Library, which is available on the DMC’s website.
